paras.urdu: عالمگیریت کے منفی اثرات (Negative Impacts of Globalization)

paras.text: Because of globalisation very negative effects are also being produced on the culture of Pakistan, like other developing countries. World institutions and their members are a means of cultural penetration in Pakistan. Their magazines, booklets, radio and television broadcasts are polluting the culture of developing countries including Pakistan. We are facing a cultural onslaught. The harms of mobile phones and the internet are hidden from no one. Religious, moral and cultural values are being uprooted. Change is clearly taking place in dress, customs, habits, language and literature, ways and lifestyle, rituals and traditions and morals etc.

paras.text: Pakistan is a developing country, and in an ordinary world economic market Pakistani goods are weak in comparison with developed countries. In this way local industry will suffer a blow. In this respect local industries will be ruined, because even within the country they cannot compete with world multinational corporations. Negative Impacts of Globalization

Because of globalisation very negative effects are also being produced on the culture of Pakistan, like other developing countries. World institutions and their members are a means of cultural penetration in Pakistan. Their magazines, booklets, radio and television broadcasts are polluting the culture of developing countries including Pakistan. We are facing a cultural onslaught. The harms of mobile phones and the internet are hidden from no one. Religious, moral and cultural values are being uprooted. Change is clearly taking place in dress, customs, habits, language and literature, ways and lifestyle, rituals and traditions and morals etc.

Pakistan is a developing country, and in an ordinary world economic market Pakistani goods are weak in comparison with developed countries. In this way local industry will suffer a blow. In this respect local industries will be ruined, because even within the country they cannot compete with world multinational corporations. International institutions give their employees big salaries and facilities which, in comparison with Pakistani institutions, are many times more and attractive. In this way balance does not remain either, and Pakistan’s experts take interest in these world institutions while they leave the national institutions. All these things are pointing to a journey towards a bad economic situation.

Essentials of Self-Reliant Economy

Self-reliance means that an individual or country depends on itself instead of depending on others. That is, it is a form of self-respect. Several basic conditions or requisites are needed for a self-reliant economic system. If these are ensured, the economic system does not depend on any particular support. The very first condition for self-reliance is that loans and aid from other nations are not expected at all. If a nation becomes addicted to this intoxication, stillness is created in its activities. Such nations go nowhere and remain waiting for loans and charity. This way of working also ends the possibilities of progress and going ahead. paras.text: … means take developing countries under their control. These financial institutions become very influential. Every aspect of the life of weak countries comes under their control. Therefore there is a need for this, that to become a dignified, free and sovereign nation, the dependence on world institutions, especially the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, be reduced and gradually ended. The best thing is that life be lived within domestic resources, i.e. there is a need to stretch one’s legs according to one’s sheet. When we go beyond our resources and do not control our unlimited desires and needs, then we have to look towards others. It is better that we learn to live within our resources; this will be useful for us. People prefer some foreign goods more. Sometimes because of the shortage or non-production of some things in the country such goods are imported. It is to be seen whether such things are necessary for remaining alive or not. If they are not a basic need, it is very good to ignore them and reduce their use. For example, Pakistan spends a large amount on the import of tea.

paras.text: To avoid dependence on others, the traditional life of ease will have to be abandoned. Every individual will have to play an active and lively role. Many changes will have to be brought, and they will have to be accepted. Hardship too will have to be borne. Everything will have to be done to live with honour and dignity. Traditionally we keep looking towards world aid, cooperation and loans. If we do not change this way and do not move ourselves, then how is self-reliance possible? The importance of the manpower of any country increases when people are technically strong and trained. For progress the support of science and technology has to be taken. Industry needs scientific thinking. To take more and useful work from people they need to be technically trained. … means take developing countries under their control. These financial institutions become very influential. Every aspect of the life of weak countries comes under their control. Therefore there is a need for this, that to become a dignified, free and sovereign nation, the dependence on world institutions, especially the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, be reduced and gradually ended. The best thing is that life be lived within domestic resources, i.e. there is a need to stretch one’s legs according to one’s sheet. When we go beyond our resources and do not control our unlimited desires and needs, then we have to look towards others. It is better that we learn to live within our resources; this will be useful for us. People prefer some foreign goods more. Sometimes because of the shortage or non-production of some things in the country such goods are imported. It is to be seen whether such things are necessary for remaining alive or not. If they are not a basic need, it is very good to ignore them and reduce their use. For example, Pakistan spends a large amount on the import of tea.

… means take developing countries under their control. These financial institutions become very influential. Every aspect of the life of weak countries comes under their control. Therefore there is a need for this, that to become a dignified, free and sovereign nation, the dependence on world institutions, especially the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank, be reduced and gradually ended. The best thing is that life be lived within domestic resources, i.e. there is a need to stretch one’s legs according to one’s sheet. When we go beyond our resources and do not control our unlimited desires and needs, then we have to look towards others. It is better that we learn to live within our resources; this will be useful for us. People prefer some foreign goods more. Sometimes because of the shortage or non-production of some things in the country such goods are imported. It is to be seen whether such things are necessary for remaining alive or not. If they are not a basic need, it is very good to ignore them and reduce their use. For example, Pakistan spends a large amount on the import of tea.

To avoid dependence on others, the traditional life of ease will have to be abandoned. Every individual will have to play an active and lively role. Many changes will have to be brought, and they will have to be accepted. Hardship too will have to be borne. Everything will have to be done to live with honour and dignity. Traditionally we keep looking towards world aid, cooperation and loans. If we do not change this way and do not move ourselves, then how is self-reliance possible? The importance of the manpower of any country increases when people are technically strong and trained. For progress the support of science and technology has to be taken. Industry needs scientific thinking. To take more and useful work from people they need to be technically trained. Unfortunately in our country the trend towards technical education is very low, which is an important obstacle in the way of economic progress. Therefore technical education is among the important requisites for self-reliance.

There is a need for increase in productive capacities within the country. Agriculture, industry and the attainment of energy will have to be taken on a priority basis. Productive capacities can be increased by bringing into use the existing resources within the country, promoting education, giving importance to science and technology and planning properly. When production increases, external dependence will automatically decrease or end. Unfortunately the people of poor and developing countries give preference to foreign goods and do not like domestic products. Another misfortune is that in these countries, because of world trade institutions, multinational corporations, free trade and globalisation, domestic products are losing their place to a dangerous extent.
